[Lecture {{< meta lecture >}}]{} ::: ::: {.my-attrib} {{< meta attribution >}} ::: ![](../../img/growth_curve_357EDD.png){.absolute bottom=30 right=0 width="400"} ::: ::: {.cell} ::: # Review ## Questions about Unit C? 1. Regression with a single continuous predictor 2. Regression with a single categorical predictor 3. Regresion with multiple predictors 4. Interaction effects with continuous predictors 5. Categorical and higher-order interactions ## Questions about Unit D? 1. Assumptions about formula and diagnostics 2. Assumptions about residuals and diagnostics 3. Polynomial regression 4. Research practices and power analysis 5. Methodological writing and reviewing # Examples ## Example 1 (Clinical/Health Psych) ::: {.fs70} > I read that doctors sometimes use the amount of beta-amyloid proteins in patient's cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to help detect Alzheimer's disease. I am interested to know if this amount is also related to patients' cognitive functioning. To investigate this, I collect CSF from and measure beta-amyloid and working memory in 120 patients with different types of dementia. Assume that both measures are continuous. ::: 1. What might the data frame look like for this study? 2. What formula would we use to test our hypothesis using LM? 3. Should we be worried about any of the LM assumptions? ## Example 2 (Sports Science) ::: {.fs70} > I want to help the tennis player I coach to improve her service return game. I suspect she struggles with faster serves and serves she tried to return backhand. To test this, I watch 70 of her recent matches and mark down the average speed of all the serves she received in that match, the percentage that she attempted to return backhand (as opposed to forehand), and the percentage that she successfully returned (as opposed to did not return). ::: 1. What might the data frame look like for this study? 2. What formula would we use to test our hypothesis using LM? 3. Should we be worried about any of the LM assumptions? ## Example 3 (Social Psych) ::: {.fs70} > I think that people at a bar will enjoy being approached by and talking with a stranger only if they find that stranger attractive, but my friend thinks that attractiveness has nothing to do with it. To test this, we observe people at a local bar and, after someone is approached by someone else, ask them if they knew that person (yes or no), how attractive they found that person (1 to 10), and how much they liked talking with that person (1 to 10). We end up with ratings from 20 participants being approached by 55 strangers and 30 friends. ::: 1. What might the data frame look like for this study? 2. What formula would we use to test our hypothesis using LM? 3. Should we be worried about any of the LM assumptions? # Activity ## Small-Group Activity **Step 1.** Write down a few of your own examples (e.g., 2 to 4). The hypotheses should be testable using one-sample $t$-tests, two-sample $t$-tests, one-way tests, or correlations. **Step 2.** Form small groups of two to three students and take turns reading each others' examples. Discuss the answers to our three questions and brainstorm together. 1. What might the data frame look like for this study? 2. What formula would we use to test our hypothesis using LM? 3. Should we be worried about any of the LM assumptions?

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
